challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.
challenge.roundIntroduction: The compliance team suspended access to the loyalty app basket feed after discovering that retention policies were not documented in the data contracts. The KPI definitions for the next promotion cycle were never formally agreed upon, leaving the team without a clear baseline for how to handle the missing personal data signals.

on_enter_ops.reason: compliance audit found missing consent fields in the schema

stalemate_ops.reason: legal team blocked KPI sign off due to unresolved data rights

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

roster.name: Automation Alex
roster.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.
roster.priorities: Building automated pipelines and maintaining full system operational stability. Ensuring seamless deployment, integration, and stability of models and services in production.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} mentioned that manual review of data contracts is sufficient for the current promotion cycle.

readings.driver: She wants the contract checks to run on their own so the team can focus on the leaflet.
readings.boundary: She will not let the promotion calendar slip for a review process.
readings.trade_off: She would accept automated contract checks if they do not stall the weekly leaflet deadline.
readings.fact: That is simply how the team handles contract reviews today.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} noted that the KPI definition process is currently done by hand.

readings.driver: She wants the KPI definitions to be generated automatically to save time.
readings.boundary: She will not agree to a KPI process that takes more than a day.
readings.trade_off: She would give up the manual KPI definition if the automated version is ready before the next promotion week.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definition works today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed that the data contracts be fully governed to enforce consent checks.

readings.driver: He wants a formal sign off on every data contract before it moves to ingestion.
readings.boundary: He will not allow any personal data to enter the pipeline without a documented consent check.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a partial review if it is the only way to keep the promotion on schedule.
readings.fact: That is simply how the data contracts are governed today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} brought up the lack of review on the hand-over from data contracts to ingestion.

readings.driver: He wants the hand-over to be automated so no one can skip the check.
readings.boundary: He will not allow the hand-over from data contracts to ingestion to run without a formal review.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a manual trigger if the review is documented.
readings.fact: That is simply how the hand-over from data contracts to ingestion works today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} suggested that the KPI definitions be formally agreed upon.

readings.driver: He wants a formal sign off on the KPI definitions so the team has a clear baseline.
readings.boundary: He will not start the next promotion cycle without agreed KPIs.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a draft KPI document if it is reviewed by the compliance team.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definitions are handled today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} mentioned that the risk assessment is currently not governed.

readings.driver: He wants the risk assessment to be fully governed to catch compliance issues early.
readings.boundary: He will not accept a risk assessment that is not reviewed by the compliance team.
readings.trade_off: He would give up the full governance on the risk assessment if the data contracts are fully governed.
readings.fact: That is simply how the risk assessment is handled today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} asked for the data contract validation and the hand-over to ingestion to run on their own.

readings.driver: He wants the data contracts and the hand-over to ingestion to be automated so the pipeline does not stall on manual checks.
readings.boundary: He will not accept a data contract process that requires a human to run it every night.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a manual trigger if the contract checks are automated.
readings.fact: That is simply how the data contracts and hand-over are handled today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} noted that the hand-over from data contracts to ingestion is currently missing.

readings.driver: He wants the hand-over to be automated so it runs without a human in the loop.
readings.boundary: He will not accept a hand-over that requires a manual request every time.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a manual trigger on the hand-over if the contract checks are automated.
readings.fact: That is simply how the hand-over from data contracts to ingestion works today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} suggested that the risk assessment be automated to reduce manual work.

readings.driver: He wants the risk assessment to be automated so it runs on a schedule.
readings.boundary: He will not accept a risk assessment that is done by hand every week.
readings.trade_off: He would give up the automation of the risk assessment if the data contracts are automated.
readings.fact: That is simply how the risk assessment is handled today.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed that the acceptance criteria be governed to ensure they are met before evaluation.

readings.driver: She wants the acceptance criteria to be reviewed so the model evaluation is reliable.
readings.boundary: She will not accept a model that goes to evaluation without reviewed acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a partial review if the criteria are clear and documented.
readings.fact: That is simply how the acceptance criteria are handled today.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} mentioned that the hand-over from acceptance criteria to model evaluation is currently not governed.

readings.driver: She wants the hand-over to be governed so the model evaluation is reliable.
readings.boundary: She will not accept a hand-over that is not reviewed by the team.
readings.trade_off: She would give up the governance on the hand-over if the acceptance criteria are governed.
